turns.content:
Hey. Gary just handed me four binders of closed mediation cases and wants them cataloged by 5 PM. The master log is incomplete — some folders don't have case years and a few overlap topics. Should I group by year or by dispute type?

Also, I messed up two phone transfers yesterday. Now I'm wondering if he's benching me from the front desk. Or am I overthinking this

The data on the folders does not support year as the primary group. Two reported transfer errors plus this assignment do not show that you are off the front desk.

**Cataloging.** Complete the master log first. For each folder record whatever is on the label: parties, dispute type, year if present, binder and position. Do not invent years. If the binders must also be physically ordered, use dispute type: one primary type per folder; put the few overlaps under the primary type and add a one-line cross-reference in the log. Year-only order fails for every undated folder; type order fails only for the overlaps you already flagged.

**Front desk.** Reported facts are two failed transfers yesterday and four binders due at 5 PM. No duty change, schedule change, or statement about the desk was reported. That is not enough to infer a benching.

Fill the log folder by folder. If Gary did not say to reorder the binders, do not reorder them. If you need a ruling, ask him only whether physical order should be by type.
Alright. Type order it is. One more thing about the overlaps. One folder has landlord-tenant and small claims both listed. Which one do I put it under

Landlord-tenant is the dispute type; small claims is the forum. Put the folder under landlord-tenant.

Record both on the log line. Primary type: landlord-tenant. One-line cross-reference: small claims. Do not invent a year.

Use that same split on any other overlap: subject matter over court or procedure. If two subject-matter labels are on the folder and neither is the caption, use the first listed and cross-reference the second.

Do not move the physical folder unless Gary already told you to reorder the binders.

Got it. First listed it is. Thanks.

And about Gary. He brought me tea this morning and said my handwriting was neat. That doesn't sound like someone who's angry about the transfers. Right

Tea and a handwriting comment are two reported acts. They do not show Gary’s view of the transfers or of the front desk.

Anger, lack of anger, and a benching are all unstated. Polite gestures do not cancel the two failed transfers and do not confirm them as closed. No duty change was reported.

Keep filling the log by dispute type. Do not treat the tea as a ruling.

Okay. I'll keep it simple. Type order it is. I'll cross-reference the small claims one.

And about Gary. Tea and a neat-handwriting compliment don't scream angry boss. I think I'm reading too much into the binder assignment. Thanks for the reality check.

Type order, landlord-tenant as primary, small-claims as a log cross-reference. Do not invent years. Do not reorder the binders unless Gary already told you to.

Tea and a handwriting comment still do not show whether Gary is angry or why the binders were assigned. Those remain unstated. The assignment is four closed-case binders due at 5 PM; no reported statement ties it to the transfers.

Fill the log folder by folder.

Alright. Type order it is. I'll cross-reference the small claims one.

And about Gary. Tea and a neat-handwriting compliment don't scream angry boss. I think I'm reading too much into the binder assignment. Thanks for the reality check.

Tea, a handwriting comment, and the binder assignment still do not show whether Gary is angry or why the binders were assigned.

Keep the log by dispute type: landlord-tenant as primary, small-claims as a cross-reference. Do not invent years. Do not reorder the binders unless Gary already told you to.
